claims.text: The starting material is high-purity, single-phase ZrB2 powder.
The intervention adds 1–2 wt.% of a boron oxide/Si precursor to ZrB2 powder.
The modified powder can be consolidated by spark plasma sintering or hot pressing at approximately 1650 °C under an inert atmosphere.
The precursor forms a uniformly distributed borosilicate interphase at ZrB2 grain boundaries.
At the sintering temperature, the boron oxide/Si precursor melts and produces a transient liquid phase.
The transient liquid phase promotes rapid densification at a lower sintering temperature.
Upon cooling, the liquid segregates to grain boundaries and solidifies as a continuous glassy borosilicate layer.
The grain-boundary borosilicate layer impedes oxygen ingress.
The grain-boundary borosilicate layer retards penetration by liquid plating metal.
The intervention refines the ZrB2 microstructure.
In-situ formation of the secondary constituent creates strong interfaces that can improve material performance.
The modified ZrB2 will achieve full densification at approximately 1650 °C.
The modified ZrB2 will have comparable or improved mechanical strength because of solid-solution effects and microstructural refinement.
The modified ZrB2 will have significantly better oxidation resistance than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
The modified ZrB2 will have significantly better liquid-metal corrosion durability than conventional single-phase ZrB2 and prior lower-temperature specimens.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 typically requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C for densification.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 has poor oxidation resistance and is vulnerable to liquid plating-metal corrosion.
The protective performance is intended to persist during oxidation in dry air up to approximately 1600 °C.
The protective performance is intended to persist during exposure to aggressive liquid-metal plating environments.
The long-term stability and large-component uniformity of the borosilicate layer remain uncertain and require experimental validation.
